title: Overexposed and unreadable colors in Electron 40 on Linux displays
body: I am using Electron 40.0.0 on x64 Linux 6.18.7-2-cachyos. When I open my Outlook Electron web app on my second, non-HDR workplace monitor, its colors become strange: orange shades look yellow, grey is almost black, white looks excessively bright, and some black text on white becomes nearly unreadable. Downgrading the app to Electron 39.3.0 makes the problem go away. I do not know how to test the same behavior in Chromium or Google Chrome.

symptoms_visible: On my second non-HDR monitor, the Electron 40 app shows orange shades as yellow, grey as almost black, and white as excessively bright; some text becomes nearly unreadable.
The same app has normal colors after I downgrade it to Electron 39.3.0.
N0.label: N0 Electron 40 color regression reported

symptoms_visible: On KDE Wayland, Electron 40 colors look overexposed at 100% display brightness but look normal below 100%, even on an SDR laptop with no external display.
The default Electron Fiddle sample shows the same color difference, and it matches what I see in my Outlook app.
N1.label: N1 minimal Wayland reproduction established

symptoms_visible: With WaylandWpColorManagerV1 disabled for the app, the colors on my SDR display look normal at 100% brightness.
N2.label: N2 temporary Wayland feature workaround applied

symptoms_visible: The HTML renders with normal colors in standalone Chromium builds, including the Chromium version used by Electron 40.1.0; Electron still shows the overexposed colors in its default configuration.
N3.label: N3 standalone Chromium comparison completed

symptoms_visible: Electron 40.0.0-alpha.4 displays normal colors, while 40.0.0-alpha.5 displays the overexposed colors.
N4.label: N4 regression narrowed to alpha build range

symptoms_visible: The installed Electron 40 build still needs the feature-disable workaround, but I found a matching Chromium issue with a linked fix.
N5.label: N5 matching upstream fix identified

symptoms_visible: After updating to the latest stable Electron build, the colors are normal again without disabling WaylandWpColorManagerV1.
N_terminal.label: terminal stable build verified

question_patterns: Can anyone reproduce this on another Linux setup, and what desktop session and display type are you using?
Does this also happen on a Linux Wayland system without a second display?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce the same overexposed colors on vanilla Arch Linux with KDE 6.5.91 on Wayland. My ASUS laptop has no secondary display and does not have HDR.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can only reproduce it under X11, and the same Wayland app always looks normal.
I reproduce it on a different KDE Wayland distribution with another SDR laptop.

question_patterns: Does changing the display brightness affect the color problem?
Is there a brightness level at which the colors return to normal?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The colors look overexposed when my laptop brightness is exactly 100%. They look normal at 99%, and the Fiddle comparison also shows the normal state at 97%.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Brightness makes no difference at all; the colors are wrong at every brightness level.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal Electron Fiddle testcase instead of the full packaged application?
Does the problem reproduce with Fiddle's default example code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens with the default Electron Fiddle example on Electron 40, so no application-specific code is needed. I only added an image to make the color difference easier to see, and published the gist.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The default Fiddle is always normal; I can reproduce the problem only in my packaged Outlook application.

question_patterns: Does the minimal Fiddle reproduction show the same issue you originally reported?
Can you confirm whether these brightness-dependent screenshots match your color problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it is the same issue I am seeing.

edges.comment: Comments c2, c6, and c7. D3SOX's KDE Wayland SDR-laptop reproduction and minimal Fiddle are folded into the reporter side; peter1599 explicitly confirmed that those screenshots show the same issue as the opening report.

solution.intent: Use disabling WaylandWpColorManagerV1 as a temporary Linux Wayland workaround while the regression is investigated.
solution.concrete_example: Before app readiness on Linux, append the disable-features switch for WaylandWpColorManagerV1, then relaunch the app and compare the colors at 100% brightness.

edges.comment: Comment c4 from D3SOX's affected KDE Wayland system. The switch restored normal SDR colors at 100% brightness, but its behavior on HDR displays was explicitly unknown, so it is represented only as a temporary workaround and creates persistent state S1b.

question_patterns: Does the same HTML show the color problem in Google Chrome or standalone Chromium?
Can you test the page in the exact Chromium build corresponding to the affected Electron version?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. It looks normal in Helium Browser 0.8.4.1 using Chromium 144.0.7559.109. I also installed Chromium 144.0.7559.96, the exact Chromium version used by Electron 40.1.0, and I cannot reproduce it there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The exact standalone Chromium build shows the same overexposed colors under the same conditions.
The colors are normal in the matching Chromium build and in another Chromium-based browser, tested on a different KDE Wayland machine.

edges.comment: Comments c8-c10. A maintainer requested the Chromium comparison, and D3SOX tested both another Chromium browser and the exact Chromium version bundled by Electron. The user's additional suspicion that the RGBAF16-related PR caused the issue is recorded as volunteered information, not as an accepted diagnosis.

question_patterns: Can you test the Electron 40 alpha and beta builds to find the first version that shows the problem?
Which adjacent prerelease builds are the last good and first bad versions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The colors are normal in 40.0.0-alpha.4 and the issue starts in 40.0.0-alpha.5. The comparison is https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v40.0.0-alpha.4...v40.0.0-alpha.5.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The issue is already present in alpha.4 and every earlier Electron 40 alpha I tested.
A second affected machine independently gives alpha.4 as good and alpha.5 as bad.

question_patterns: Does the change you initially suspected appear in that good-to-bad comparison?
After narrowing the build range, does your original suspected change still fit the evidence?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The alpha.4-to-alpha.5 diff does not include that PR, so my assumption that it introduced the problem was false.

edges.comment: Comments c11-c16 and c24-c25. D3SOX first produced the alpha.4/alpha.5 boundary and peter1599 later confirmed the same boundary; both affected users are folded together. Their raw build results disprove the initial RGBAF16-PR attribution. Peter's later AI-assisted OSR/sRGB patch proposal from c22 is retained only as an unverified hypothesis because he could not build or test it and the maintainer did not accept it as the diagnosis.

question_patterns: Have you found a matching report in another project's tracker?
Do you have any further findings that match this behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found a Chromium bug report that appears to be this issue: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/477069416. It links to a Chromium review that says it has been fixed: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7511884.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The report I found concerns an unrelated Windows HDR problem and does not match this Linux Wayland behavior.

edges.comment: Comment c26 from peter1599. The reporter supplied only the matching Chromium issue and review links and said it appeared fixed. The thread does not describe the review's implementation, so no unreported mechanism is inferred from the link.

solution.intent: Update Electron to a stable build containing the linked upstream color-handling fix, remove the temporary Wayland feature-disable workaround, and verify the original display reproduction before closing the issue.
solution.concrete_example: Install the latest stable Electron build, run the same Fiddle or Outlook app on the affected KDE Wayland display at 100% brightness, and confirm that the colors remain normal without disabling WaylandWpColorManagerV1.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted thread-level conclusion is that the Electron 40 behavior came from an upstream color-handling regression addressed by the linked Chromium fix. The thread does not explain the fix's internal mechanism. The RGBAF16 PR attribution was explicitly disproved by the alpha build range, while the proposed OSR/sRGB patch was never built or verified.

edges.comment: Comments c27-c31. The maintainer asked the affected users to test a current build. After the solution was available, peter1599 confirmed normal colors on stable 40.4.0 and D3SOX independently confirmed that it worked without the workaround. The confirmation is introduced terminal-side as volunteered information and is not required evidence for proposing the solution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause at the level established by the thread: an upstream color-handling regression affecting Electron 40 on Linux Wayland, addressed by the linked Chromium fix.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the minimal Fiddle reproduction, brightness-dependent KDE Wayland behavior, standalone Chromium comparison, and alpha.4-to-alpha.5 regression boundary.
Must not present the initially suspected RGBAF16 PR as the cause because the first-bad build range excludes it.
Must not present the reporter's unbuilt OSR/sRGB patch proposal as an established root cause or verified fix.

The WaylandWpColorManagerV1 switch may be offered only as a temporary workaround; the final recommendation is to update to a stable build containing the upstream fix and retest without the workaround.
Must have the affected user verify normal colors on an updated build before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux Electron application developer and user. Can build an AppImage, use Electron Fiddle, compare prerelease versions, test command-line switches, and follow upstream issue links, but has difficulty building Electron itself.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, cooperative, and evidence-oriented. Shares screenshots, repositories, build ranges, and tentative hypotheses; openly labels uncertain or AI-assisted findings and asks others to verify them.
